messages.subject: Compiled Function Aborts R
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am really new to nimble and I am trying to write a nimble function to get around dynamic indexing. I have this function working in the R version; however, when I compile it, it aborts R when trying to run it. I have seen some stuff talking about NAs vs NaN and that indexing likely aborts R. I have tried trouble shooting it but I have not been able to square it away as of yet. Could someone look this over and see if I have done something wrong? Thank you for any help.

# Vector UCH
UCH_vec <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
    records = double(0), # Number of animals
    left = double(1), # When they enter study
    right = double(1), # When they leave study
    log_haz = double(1), # log hazard rate
    beta_manage = double(0), # management effect
    manage = double(1), # indicator for management
    maxright = double(0)){ # Last month of study
    # Create UCH and SLR
    UCH <- nimMatrix(value = NaN,
                     nrow = records,
                     ncol = maxright)
    SLR <- nimNumeric(value = NaN)
    for(j in 1:records){
      for(k in left[j] : right[j]){
        UCH[j, k] <- exp(log_haz[k] + beta_manage * manage[j])
      }
      SLR[j] <- exp(-sum(UCH[j, left[j] : right[j]]))
    }
    return(SLR)
    returnType(double(1))
  }
)

messages.author: 2a8058139b2abd61
messages.subject: Re: Compiled Function Aborts R
parts: For everyone that may run into this problem in the future, I did not size the vector for SLR correctly. R automatically sizes them; however, the backend C++ appears not to and that is documented here: https://r-nimble.org/html_manual/cha-RCfunctions.html.  Changing the vector to the output length needed fixed the problem.
